title: The Power of Purposeful Practice
coreMove: Replace broad repetition with one narrow, feedback-rich target that forces the next attempt to change.
sourcePressure: The opening chapter introduces purposeful practice through Steve Faloon digit-memory training and contrasts naive repetition with specific goals, focus, feedback, stretch, and method changes after plateaus.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says more repetitions plus consistency equals improvement.

sourceAnchors.name: Steve Faloon
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen sidecar ties chapter 1 to Faloon digit-memory training as the concrete case for purposeful practice, specific goals, feedback, stretch, and method changes after plateaus
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Steve Faloon did not improve by admiring memory in general; the digit string got longer because each miss told the next attempt where to work.

hook: another musician replaying a whole piece
counterintuition: hard work beats talent in a generic way
tryThisNow: repeat the skill until it feels better
examples: violin weak bar from old Peak draft
sales pitch pricing objection from old modern package

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: amateur archery sight adjustment at an indoor range
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who keeps shooting full rounds and calling every miss random
exampleSpecs.stakes: a qualifying score keeps slipping because the same leftward miss survives every practice night
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah stops the full round, tapes a palm-sized target over the left edge, shoots only five arrows, and writes the sight correction before the next five arrows leave the bow
exampleSpecs.firstImage: paper target faces clipped in a row under buzzing range lights

exampleSpecs.domain: trial paralegal exhibit labeling before a hearing
exampleSpecs.audience: a detail-oriented worker who keeps rereading the whole packet
exampleSpecs.stakes: one mislabeled exhibit could slow a judge during a short motion window
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Thomas finds that every returned packet failed at the date stamp, covers the rest of the binder, and drills only the stamp check until the next packet changes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three rejected exhibit tabs lined beside a blue date stamp

exampleSpecs.domain: espresso bar milk texture training during a quiet prep hour
exampleSpecs.audience: a barista promoted too soon who keeps making passable drinks
exampleSpecs.stakes: the cafe loses regulars when every cappuccino looks acceptable but tastes thin
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Camille pours three ounces into a marked tasting cup, listens for the hiss pitch, and compares the foam line before steaming the next pitcher
exampleSpecs.firstImage: steam fog curling around a row of stainless tasting cups

exampleSpecs.domain: museum docent practicing one transition between galleries
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer who thinks a full tour run is the responsible way to prepare
exampleSpecs.stakes: visitors keep drifting away at the same gallery doorway
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Jonas asks a senior docent to interrupt the exact sentence where visitors drift, rewrites only that doorway transition, and walks it twice before touching the rest of the tour
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a security rope brushing the floor between two gallery rooms

exampleSpecs.domain: rowing coxswain call timing on a cold practice launch
exampleSpecs.audience: a team leader whose commands are energetic but late
exampleSpecs.stakes: the crew loses rhythm before race weekend because corrections arrive after the stroke has already passed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 6:18 a.m., Giulia records ten strokes, marks the late calls with pencil ticks, and repeats only the call before the catch until the next set lands earlier
exampleSpecs.firstImage: pencil ticks beside stroke numbers on a damp clipboard

exampleSpecs.domain: software debugger learning one failing unit test
exampleSpecs.audience: a junior developer who keeps scanning the whole repository
exampleSpecs.stakes: a release branch stays blocked while the same edge case fails
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lin hides every passing test, prints the failing input on a sticky note, changes one parser branch, and reruns only that unit before touching the rest of the suite
exampleSpecs.firstImage: one red test name glowing above a stack of green checks

skillTargets: identify purposeful practice rather than naive repetition
choose a narrow target after a plateau
explain why feedback must change the next attempt
use Steve Faloon as a practice-loop example without overclaiming memory genius

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one skill you planned to rehearse broadly. Name the exact miss from the last attempt, choose the next three reps that expose only that miss, and decide what signal will make rep four different.
